capitals.name: Mekelle
capitals.note: 'Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region' fell to federal forces on 28 November 2020 and was retaken by the TDF on 28 June 2021. Coordinates are the researcher's; Mekelle is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the Tigray Region, contested between the TPLF and the federal government

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: from 3 November 2020 the Tigray Region is the ground of the rebel government; the federal side held the main roads and cities after the fall of Mekelle on 28 November, so the whole region is a contested zone (ledger contest events). Cliopatria has no row for this state.

correction.text: most of the Tigray Region without the Eritrean-held north and without Western Tigray, held by Amhara regional authorities (gazetteer name 'Western Tigray' still to be added); held by the TDF from late June 2021

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after 28 June 2021 'the TDF now controlled most of the Tigray region'; Amhara and Eritrean forces held parts 'in the west and north, respectively'. The north is cut with a band along the Eritrean frontier (the researcher's reading); the west is now subtracted by the name 'Western Tigray' (Amhara-held from November 2020; the gazetteer entry is still to be added). The page gives no area. Reviewer round: valid for 2021-2022; Shire is lost in October 2022 (see the 2023 keyframe).

correction.text: the TDF-held part of Tigray after the loss of Shire in October 2022: Tigray without the Eritrean-held north, without Western Tigray (Amhara-held) and without Shire

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (reviewer round): the 2021-2022 shape without Shire, taken by Eritrea and Ethiopia on 17 October 2022 ('that same day, the strategic city of Shire was taken by Eritrea and Ethiopia'); it holds to the Interim Regional Administration of 23 March 2023.

region.text: the Tigray Region, governed by the TPLF

ledger.note: 3 November 2020: the Tigrayan forces attack the federal Northern Command and the Tigray War begins. The war 'lasted from 3 November 2020'; Tigrayan forces attacked Northern Command bases just before midnight on 3 November. The page names the Tigray Region, governed by the Tigray People's Liberation Front, as the ground; the rebel state is read from the first day of the war.

November 2020: the federal government and its allies fight the Tigrayan forces for the Tigray Region. 'Federal allied forces captured Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region, on 28 November'; in February 2021 a UN official said 'up to 40% of Tigray was not controlled by Ethiopian troops'. The year of the Mekelle sentence is read from the war's start.

region.text: most of the Tigray Region without the Eritrean-held north and without Western Tigray, held by Amhara regional authorities (gazetteer name 'Western Tigray' still to be added); held by the TDF from late June 2021

ledger.note: 28 June 2021: the Tigray Defense Forces retake Mekelle and hold most of Tigray. 'On 28 June 2021, the Tigray Defense Forces retook the city of Mekelle'; the International Crisis Group said 'the TDF now controlled most of the Tigray region'; in April 2021 they had held rural central and southern Tigray and parts of the east, 'while the ENDF was in control of the main roads and urban areas'. Reviewer af-01-c: confidence lowered to 2 because the region included Western Tigray, now subtracted by name (gazetteer entry to be added); the Tigray War page the Tigray War infobox says was 'ceded and occupied by neighboring Amhara regional authorities' from November 2020.

region.text: the Awra and Chifra districts of Afar near the Amhara border

ledger.note: 17-19 July 2021: the TDF attack into Afar. 'From 17 to 19 July, the TDF began launching attacks in the Afar Region to its east'; on 13 October 2021 fighting 'resumed in Afar, within the Awra and Chifra districts near the Amhara border'; 'Heavy fighting in western Afar displaced over 54,000 people'. The page speaks of attacks and fighting, not of captured towns, so the Afar edge is the researcher's reading of the land the TDF held (page silent on the extent).

region.text: Lalibela and Weldiya in North Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: August 2021: the TDF take Lalibela and Weldiya. 'The next day, Lalibela was reported to have been seized by Tigrayan forces' (the sentence before is dated 4 August 2021); 'the city of Weldiya was captured by the TDF on 12 August 2021'. Amhara Region land outside the Tigray contest zone.

region.text: Dessie and Kombolcha in South Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: 30-31 October 2021: the TDF take Dessie and Kombolcha. 'On 30 October, it was reported that Dessie had fallen to the TDF'; 'On 31 October, the TDF claimed to have captured Kombolcha, a town 21 km (13 mi) east of Dessie'.

region.text: the Awra and Chifra districts of Afar near the Amhara border

ledger.note: 20 December 2021: the TDF withdraw from Afar and Amhara. 'On 20 December 2021, the TPLF announced they had withdrawn their troops from Amhara and Afar'.

region.text: Lalibela and Weldiya in North Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: December 2021: Lalibela and Weldiya are no longer held. The Ethiopian government said it had 'recaptured several towns in the Amhara and Afar regions including Lalibela and Shewa Robit' (26 November-6 December 2021); the page gives no date for Weldiya; 'On 20 December 2021, the TPLF announced they had withdrawn their troops from Amhara and Afar'. December is the page's date of the withdrawal.

region.text: Dessie and Kombolcha in South Wollo, Amhara Region

ledger.note: 6 December 2021: government forces retake Dessie and Kombolcha. 'On 6 December, government forces claimed to have recaptured the strategic cities of Dessie and Kombolcha.'

region.text: Shire (Inda Selassie), the strategic city of western-central Tigray

ledger.note: 17 October 2022: federal and Eritrean forces take Shire from the TDF. 'that same day, the strategic city of Shire was taken by Eritrea and Ethiopia, leading to the evacuation of thousands of its inhabitants'; the TDF had entered Shire on 30 June 2021 'after it had been abandoned by Eritrean troops'. The 50 km radius is the researcher's reading.

2 November 2022: the Pretoria cessation of hostilities. Ethiopia and the TPLF 'signed an agreement for a cessation of hostilities', effective 3 November; talks had started in Pretoria on 25 October 2022; Eritrea 'were not involved in the agreement'.

region.text: the TDF-held part of Tigray after the loss of Shire in October 2022: Tigray without the Eritrean-held north, without Western Tigray (Amhara-held) and without Shire

ledger.note: 23 March 2023: the Tigray authority becomes the federal Interim Regional Administration. The infobox: 'Interim Regional Administration of Tigray formed on 23 March 2023'; the page does not say who held Tigray's land between the cessation of hostilities and that date.

region.text: the TDF-held part of Tigray after the loss of Shire in October 2022: Tigray without the Eritrean-held north, without Western Tigray (Amhara-held) and without Shire

ledger.note: 23 March 2023: the rebel state ends as the Interim Regional Administration of Tigray is formed. Eritrea 'largely continued to occupy parts of Tigray as of 2023' and Western Tigray stayed under Amhara regional authorities. The TPLF page (Tigray People's Liberation Front) adds that Ethiopia's parliament designated it a terrorist organization in 2021 and removed it from that list on 22 March 2023.

wars.name: Tigray War
wars.outcome: Cessation of hostilities signed 2 November 2022 in Pretoria; the Interim Regional Administration of Tigray formed on 23 March 2023; Western Tigray 'ceded and occupied by neighboring Amhara regional authorities'; Eritrea occupying parts as of 2023.
wars.note: The TDF advanced into Afar (from 17-19 July 2021) and took Weldiya on 12 August 2021, then announced the withdrawal of its troops from Amhara and Afar on 20 December 2021. Shire was taken by Eritrea and Ethiopia in October 2022.

certainty.note: The front lines of the Tigray War moved month by month; the page gives no boundary for the TDF-held area.

sources.title: Tigray War
sources.note: Start 3 November 2020, Mekelle 28 November 2020 and 28 June 2021, areas held by the TDF, Amhara and Eritrean forces, Pretoria 2 November 2022, Interim Regional Administration 23 March 2023.

sources.title: Tigray People's Liberation Front
sources.note: Opened in the reviewer round for the identity: founded 18 February 1975, headquarters Mekelle, alternative names (Woyane), terrorist designation 2021 withdrawn 22 March 2023, TDF entry into Afar and Amhara in July 2021 and the ENDF counter-offensive by December 2021. The page content shows no Wikidata Q-number (wikidata.org is unreachable), so wikidata stays null.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks: the Tigray People's Liberation Front held 'most of the Tigray region' from late June 2021 to the cessation of hostilities of 2 November 2022, over a year, so it gets a dossier of type rebel. Written from one page (the Tigray War page, opened for the Ethiopia dossier); no TPLF or Tigray Defense Forces article was opened, so wikipedia and wikidata are null and the name is the researcher's. Amhara forces held Western Tigray (Welkait, Tselemti, Raya) and Eritrean forces the north; neither is carved out exactly (the north by a band along the Eritrean frontier, the west not at all, for lack of a gazetteer name 'Western Tigray'). The page does not say who held Tigray's land between 2 November 2022 and 23 March 2023. Gazetteer names needed: Mekelle (place), Western Tigray, Welkait (regions). Reviewer round (af-01-c-fixed): the TPLF article was opened (founded 18 February 1975, headquarters Mekelle; Woyane), so wikipedia is filled; wikidata stays null because the page content carries no Q-number and wikidata.org is unreachable. Western Tigray (Amhara-held from November 2020) is subtracted by name from the 2021 keyframe, the 2021 gain, the 2023 loss and the dissolve (gazetteer entry still to be added). Mirror of the Ethiopia dossier: the TDF occupation of Afar and Amhara land in 2021 (three spans: Afar edge from July, confidence 1; Lalibela and Weldiya from August; Dessie and Kombolcha from 30-31 October; all ended by 20 December 2021) and the loss of Shire on 17 October 2022, with a new 2023 keyframe without Shire. Gazetteer names needed: Western Tigray, Weldiya, Kombolcha, Chifra, Shire, Mekelle.
